q: We introduce SWE-Maintain, 100 three-event maintenance episodes reconstructed from 50 real-world Python repositories
r: Include: paired evaluation design is the main contribution (EC6 ii), tasks extend or modify code over episodes, not pure issue repair.

q: Median observations contain 118–286 tokens
r: EC6: cost analysis of published SWE-bench trajectories (issue repair), not a code-development evaluation.

q: We presented ANCHOR, a benchmark that reframes evaluation in agentic coding from task completion alone to task completion under explicit engineering constraints.
r: Include: new benchmark and trajectory-grounded evaluation of constraint following on repository tasks across 19 agent configurations (EC6 ii).

q: We identify Starting-State Robustness, the ability to maintain performance on a task when the starting state already contains earlier work on that task
r: Include: new evaluation dimension and benchmark comparing five agents from clean and residual starts (EC6 ii).

q: Coding agents increasingly undertake development tasks in mature enterprise repositories, yet existing benchmarks offer limited insight into whether they fulfill complete Product Requirement Documents (PRDs)
r: Include: PACE-Bench evaluates agents building to full PRDs at feature level and contributes an evaluation methodology.

q: coding benchmark task (e.g SWE-Bench)
r: EC6: tasks are SWE-Bench style issue repair, driven by a user simulator; issue repair is always excluded.

q: We used Claude Code to migrate ten PyTorch research projects from GPUs to TPUs
r: EC6: a specialised-domain task (GPU-to-TPU migration of research code), neither feature-level building from requirements nor an evaluation-method contribution.

q: We qualitatively annotated 325 experiments reported in 146 peer-reviewed full papers published between 2025 and 2026.
r: Include: secondary study of how agentic coding evaluations control harness, model and cost, directly relevant to RQ3.

q: Second, we introduce Foresight-SWE, a benchmark built from real PR pairs where an initial change introduces a defect that is repaired only by a later PR.
r: EC6: SWE-bench style benchmark mined from PR pairs and fixes, i.e. defect repair, not feature or project building.

q: SWEBench (Jimenez et al., 2024) for code repair, SWT-Bench (Mündler et al., 2024) for test case generation
r: EC6: harness self-evolution studied on issue repair and test generation datasets; not application development.

q: We construct realistic compiler construction workflows with strict serial dependencies
r: Include: long-horizon compiler construction with cost, quality and robustness metrics for comparing agents; project-level and evaluation-method contribution.

q: For code review, we use the patch-level review dataset released with Hydra-Reviewer
r: EC6: code generation on LiveCodeBench problems and code review; small tasks and code review, not application development.

q: We study how token cost in agentic coding varies across programming languages, controlling for problem difficulty
r: Include: controlled comparison of coding agents and models with cost metrics and trajectory analysis, so the evaluation method is the contribution (tasks are small, borderline).

q: We introduced MT-Web2Code, the first multi-turn multimodal benchmark for iterative web UI coding
r: Include: new benchmark with evaluation protocol for coding agents editing web page code (EC6 ii).

q: We present GenXR-Bench, the first benchmark to evaluate the functional and interactive correctness of agent-generated XR software.
r: EC6: benchmark limited to one specialised domain (XR development within XR Blocks), not an evaluation-method contribution for general code development.

q: A dynamic, trace-driven evaluation paradigm. We introduce evaluation-as-construction
r: Include: new trace-driven, rubric-based evaluation method for coding agents on real user tasks, so the contribution is the evaluation method.

q: FullStack-Bench, a novel benchmark that comprehensively evaluates the functionalities of the generated full-stack websites
r: Include: builds full-stack applications from requirements and contributes a new benchmark, so not only a new agent on an existing benchmark.

q: Our study focuses on one competition-level benchmark, one execution-feedback scaffold, and W4A16 quantization, with Python as the solution language.
r: EC6: tasks are competition-level programming problems, not application code development.

q: we propose an execution control harness that tightly couples LLM-based code generation with governed execution.
r: Include: YAML workflow harness for coding agents compared against a GitHub Spec Kit baseline under identical conditions in an industrial case study.

q: This paper presents Spec-Driven AI, a multiagent framework for specification-centric Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) automation.
r: Include: spec-driven multi-agent SDLC framework with governed context via MCP; tool-demo paper describing the approach.

q: We present a specification-driven governance framework that treats the specification as the primary governance artifact and the shared contract for human–AI collaboration.
r: Include: specification-driven governance of AI-generated code with a spec review gate, approved baseline and a controlled human study (group a).

q: strict decoupling of pedagogical specification from implementation
r: Include: spec-first agentic coding workflow (specification, acceptance tests, approval gates) run with Claude Code, Codex and others, in three case studies (group a).

q: We conducted two studies comparing non-governed and governed AI-assisted development: bootstrapping a new project (Setup) and implementing a complex feature (Extension).
r: Include: schema and contract as source of truth with guardrails for coding agents, compared against a non-governed baseline on project and feature tasks (group a).

q: ACM, New York, NY, USA, 2 pages.
r: EC3: two-page ICSE-Companion vision paper with hypotheses and a research agenda, no agent evaluated.

q: shifts the developer’s focus from writing low-level code to designing high-level
r: Include: SysSpec specification-driven LLM code generation and evolution; this is the journal version, so the arXiv record rayyan-800486075 carries EC4 (group a).

q: This paper introduces command coding, a structured methodology that applies traditional software engineering management principles
r: Include: plan-and-review methodology for orchestrating coding agents, related to SDD, with a production case study measuring effort and quality (group a).

q: Agent manifests are project-speciﬁc instruction ﬁles providing AI coding agents with conventions, structure, and behavioural constraints.
r: Include: content analysis of 80 CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md-style manifests for coding agents (group b).

q: In this paper, we study how open-source projects organize these guidance files and how they communicate testing expectations to coding agents.
r: Include: empirical study of AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md files for coding agents (group b).

q: A 142-day, 297-commit longitudinal experience report
r: Include: framework of agent-loaded knowledge, rules, skills and AGENTS.md for AI-driven development with Claude Code, plus an experience report (group b); short but a full paper.

q: By employing different prompts (with or without context), we conclude the advantages of contextrich prompts for autonomous agents.
r: Include: Auto-GPT builds a web application from requirements and the study compares context-rich against high-level prompts, so a feature or project-level evaluation (group c); short ASE paper but not EC3.

q: we analyzed 91 project-level rule files for coding agents at Google, a global technology company
r: Include: taxonomy derived from developer-written rule files for coding agents (group b).

q: This paper argues that the central challenge is coordination: deciding who does what, when, and under whose authority.
r: IC1: conceptual position paper on governance of agentic software engineering; not SDD, context files or an evaluation of coding agents.

q: The systematic review is a summary of literature on the agentic software engineering methodologies, frameworks, and techniques published in 2022-2025.
r: Include: secondary study of agentic software engineering, a source of approaches and gaps.
